vectors.name: non_bmp_key_ordering
vectors.why: RFC 8785 sorts object members by UTF-16 code units. A key above U+FFFF is encoded as a surrogate pair, so it sorts BELOW U+FF5E by code unit and above it by code point. An implementation sorting by code point produces different bytes for this object -- and therefore a different block_id for identical knowledge.

vectors.name: nfc_form
vectors.why: The composed form of a string the next vector carries decomposed. The protocol normalizes nothing, so these are two different values and MUST produce two different digests. Pair with nfd_form.

vectors.name: nfd_form
vectors.why: The decomposed form. Identical when rendered, distinct as bytes, and therefore a distinct block. An implementation that normalized on the way in would silently merge two blocks a user wrote separately.

vectors.name: duplicate_key_document
vectors.why: JSON parsers differ on duplicate keys and most take the last. A document that says two things about one member has no single reading, so it MUST be rejected at decode rather than resolved by whichever parser is in use.

vectors.name: lone_surrogate
vectors.why: An unpaired surrogate is not a character and has no UTF-8 encoding, so it cannot be canonicalized. Rejected rather than replaced, because a replacement character would change the value silently.
